section_summary: This section finishes an account of Japanese monitoring of Allied radio traffic, then examines Japanese naval intelligence, purchasing organizations, and contacts with Soviet residents in Shanghai. Appendices provide organization charts, a Manwa employee list, and biographies of China Seas Fleet officers. The final pages begin an investigation of Eugene Hovans and his work for the Japanese Naval Liaison Office.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese naval radio monitoring and intelligence organizations
subfiles.about: The report describes Allied radio interception, Japanese naval listening posts, intelligence and purchasing organizations, and contacts with Soviets in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The opening pages finish a firsthand account of radio monitoring in Manila and Shanghai during Allied raids and landings, including equipment, procedures, and perceived Japanese failures. Subsequent sections describe listening-post personnel, the division of intelligence responsibilities between Tokyo and Shanghai, and Navy-connected organizations including Manwa, Sakura Kikan, Kodama Kikan, and Agmol. The report closes with Japanese attempts to cultivate and obtain information from Soviet residents and institutions in Shanghai.

subfiles.about: Identifies Manwa's directors and employees by department, with residences, prefectures, and some telephone numbers.
subfiles.summary: The roster names Manwa's managing director, director, department heads, and staff in its executive, business, and finance departments. It includes residential addresses and telephone numbers for several senior personnel, as well as employees' stated places of origin.

subfiles.about: Charts Kodama Kikan's purchasing and funding relationships with Japanese naval aviation and China Seas Fleet offices.
subfiles.summary: Shows supervisory, purchasing, remittance, and branch-office links for the Kodama organization.

subfiles.title: Biographical data: outstanding officers of the Japanese China Seas Fleet
subfiles.about: Provides career histories of senior officers attached to the China Seas Fleet and related naval offices.
subfiles.summary: Individual biographies trace officers' schooling, promotions, sea assignments, specialist duties, and postings in China and Japan. The entries cover fleet commanders and staff, Shanghai naval landing and liaison offices, paymasters, medical personnel, and a construction officer.

subfiles.title: Contents for Eugene Hovans appendix
subfiles.about: Lists the introduction, personal history, Manila mission, and conclusion of the Hovans investigation.
subfiles.summary: Provides headings and internal page references for the Hovans appendix.

subfiles.title: Eugene Hovans: introduction and background
subfiles.about: Investigates Eugene Hovans's history, Japanese naval employment, informants, and alleged intelligence and criminal activities.
subfiles.summary: The report compares Japanese naval officers' description of Hovans as a minor information broker with outside claims that he ran a consequential intelligence network. It recounts his earlier work, murder conviction, release by Japanese forces, and employment on the Russian desk in Shanghai. It summarizes an embedded December 12, 1945 Japanese naval statement, letters attributed to Hovans, and interviews with Nanba and Fukuhara. A long statement by German agent Frederick Wiehl alleges informant networks, racketeering, violence, and a mission to penetrate Allied intelligence in Manila; the Manila mission section begins on page 166.
